goals.scale: 500 columns x 100,000 rows. Initial render under 500ms, scrolling at about 60 frames per second on a normal laptop, search and filter results under 200ms.
goals.versioning: 0.x versions until all core features are done. Breaking changes are allowed in 0.x. Then 1.0 with semantic versioning.

priorities.later: Wanted, low priority. Can come after 1.0.
priorities.future: Optional. Only if a real need appears.

rules.workOrder: Do core features first, then later, then future. Inside a priority, a feature comes after the features in its dependsOn. If this does not decide the order, follow the order of this list.
rules.acceptance: Acceptance items and tasks of a feature are written together with the user when work on the feature starts.
rules.passes: A feature has passes: true only when every acceptance item has an automated test that passes. The test name starts with the feature id, for example "FEAT-007: a column can have the type number". Layout items use browser tests, speed items use the benchmark script. If a test of a feature fails, its passes value goes back to false.

features.title: Base layout
features.why: A table with fixed column widths that scrolls in both directions.
acceptance: Each column uses its own width or the default width, and the table width is the sum of the column widths
With maxVisibleHeight, rows scroll inside the container
The header stays visible while rows scroll
Overlay scroll bars do not cover the last column or the last row when scrolled to the end
A table with no columns shows a "No columns" message

features.title: Library build and package
features.why: Other apps must be able to install the library from npm.

features.title: Rendering spike: <table> or <div> grid
features.why: Virtual rendering of rows and columns, pinned columns and column groups all depend on the DOM structure. Decide it with data before building features.
acceptance: A native <table> version and a <div> grid version are both measured at 500 columns x 100,000 rows, and the choice is made from the numbers

features.title: Test setup for browser and speed tests
features.why: jsdom does no layout, so layout and speed acceptance items need a real browser. Without these tests, no such item can pass.
acceptance: Layout acceptance items can be tested with browser tests (Playwright)
Speed acceptance items can be tested with a benchmark script
Browser tests can check the UI with axe
tasks: Add this rule to CLAUDE.md: all UI that the library renders must meet WCAG 2.2 level AA, and browser tests check each feature's UI with axe

features.title: Virtual rendering
features.why: Only the rows and columns on screen are rendered, so the table stays fast at full scale.
acceptance: The table shows 500 columns x 100,000 rows and meets the scale goals

features.title: Data pipeline and state model
features.why: Search, filters, sort and pagination must work together in a fixed order.
acceptance: Rows go through fixed steps in the browser, which a server mode can take over later

features.title: Column types and custom cell render
features.why: Dates, numbers and badges need formatting, and filters, sort and export need to know each column's type.
acceptance: A column can have the type text, number, date or category
A column can have a custom render function or formatter

features.title: Theming with CSS variables
features.why: Apps must be able to match the table to their own design.
acceptance: All colors, borders, spacing and fonts come from --wide-table-* variables with defaults

features.title: UI text overrides
features.why: The built-in UI has its own text, such as "No columns" and filter labels. A public library must let apps change it, for example for other languages.

features.title: Sorting
features.why: Users need to order rows by a column.

features.title: Pinned columns
features.why: In a wide table, key columns such as ID or name must stay visible while the user scrolls right.
acceptance: A column pinned to the left or the right stays in place during horizontal scrolling

features.title: Column groups
features.why: Hundreds of columns are easier to read and use in named groups.
acceptance: Groups in the column config can have several levels
A group can be expanded and collapsed in the UI
A collapsed group shows only the columns marked as its summary
A collapsed group with no summary column shows as one narrow column with its name

features.title: Hide and show columns
features.why: With hundreds of columns, users must choose which ones they see.
acceptance: The user can hide and show columns from the UI
A columns tool panel shows all columns as a tree with their groups, with show and hide checkboxes and a search box

features.title: Free text search
features.why: Users need to find rows without knowing which column has the value.
acceptance: One search box searches the whole table
Search uses the shown text of visible columns only
Results show in under 200ms at full scale

features.title: Column filters
features.why: Users need to narrow rows by the values of one column.
acceptance: Text and category columns have a value list filter with a checkbox for each unique value and a search box
Number and date columns have a condition filter
Filter results show in under 200ms at full scale

features.title: Row actions
features.why: Apps need buttons per row, such as Edit, which opens the app's own modal.
acceptance: An actions column, pinned right, shows the buttons from the config
A button click calls onRowAction with the row

features.title: Documentation
features.why: A public library needs docs to be used by others.

features.title: Pagination
features.why: Some apps want pages instead of one long scrolling list.
acceptance: Pagination is an optional mode. Without it, the table is one scrolling list

features.title: Status bar
features.why: Users need to see how many rows match.
acceptance: A footer shows the total row count and the row count after filters

features.title: CSV export
features.why: Users need to take the data they see to Excel or other tools.
acceptance: The export has the current view: filtered and sorted rows, and the visible columns only

features.title: Resize columns
features.why: Users want to change column widths by dragging.
acceptance: Dragging the edge of a header changes the column width

features.title: Reorder columns
features.why: Users want to change the column order by dragging.
acceptance: Dragging a header moves the column
A column cannot be moved out of its group

features.title: Row selection
features.why: Users want to select rows and act on them.
acceptance: A checkbox column selects rows
A select all checkbox selects all rows
The app can get the selected rows

features.title: Keyboard navigation
features.why: Users who do not use a mouse must be able to move between cells.
acceptance: The arrow keys move the focus between cells

features.title: Row grouping
features.why: Group rows by the value of one column.
acceptance: Rows can be grouped by the values of one column

features.title: Multi-level row grouping with totals
features.why: Group by several columns and show totals such as sum and average in group rows.

features.title: Master/detail
features.why: A row expands to show a detail panel below it.

features.title: Server-side data mode
features.why: Support data sets too large for the browser.

features.title: Built-in row edit modal
features.why: Apps that do not want their own form could use a form generated from the column types.
